deck_title: Rankine-Kaufmann finite-core vortex regularization vs naive 1/r point-vortex slingshot rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic William John Macquorn Rankine (1858) & Walter Kaufmann (1962) / Scully (1975) algebraic finite-core vortex regularization (enclosed Stokes circulation Gamma(r) = Gamma_inf * r^2 / (r^2 + r_c^2) and tangential velocity v_theta = (Gamma_inf / (2*pi)) * r / (r^2 + r_c^2), locking velocity ratio v/v_exact = 1.0000x across all 17 radial stations u = (r_c/r)^2 in [0.000, 1.000] with 0/17 violated) versus naive singular Biot-Savart 1/r point-vortex velocity (v_naive = Gamma_inf / (2*pi*r), which overshoots tangential speed by 1 + (r_c/r)^2 = 1 + u to 1.2500x at S4, 1.5000x at S8, and 2.0000x / 4x centrifugal acceleration at core boundary S16 across 16/17 stations) and 64-ring Stokes vorticity circulation quadrature.

cards.headline: Exact controls are useful; realism remains a separate job.
good_fit: Tornado funnels, aircraft wingtip contrails, smoke rings, and magical swirl particle systems
Regularizing singular Biot-Savart 1/r vortex filaments via r/(r^2 + r_c^2) so near-core particles orbit smoothly in solid-body rotation instead of slinging outward like shrapnel
Computing smooth tangential advection without square roots using squared distance r^2 = dx^2 + dz^2
not_for: Uniform rectilinear wind fields with zero vorticity curl (omega = 0)
Static architectural meshes with no particle or fluid advection
